findings.text: the new sentence "The warm solve's own arithmetic still has to fall about sixfold under either bound" does not follow from the numbers the same sentence cites: a warm stationary-point solve of 0.63–0.82 ms held to a 0.2 ms per-slice bound is a three- to four-fold fall (0.634/0.2 = 3.2, 0.817/0.2 = 4.1), while six-fold is 1.225/0.2, the whole-call ratio; and the sentence's own amortization claim contradicts it, because if batching 16 slices shares the launches across slices then the per-slice cost falls toward the solve's arithmetic and no six-fold arithmetic reduction is owed, whereas if the solve is arithmetic-bound rather than launch-bound then batching does not share its cost and the required fall is three- to four-fold, not six — the section cannot hold both, and which regime the 55 launches sit in is exactly what the previous review found unstated
